terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the accusative and an infinitive or ut
evidence: Ter. And. 780–781: coāctus lēgibus eam uxōrem dūcet
Verg. Ecl. 2.7: morī mē dēnique cōgēs?
terms.comment: coāctus, against one’s will; “I was forced to” is coāctus sum with an infinitive.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with ad or in
terms.comment: Of driving someone into doing something: aliquem ad aliquid compellere.

phrases.latin: nīl nostrī miserēre? morī mē dēnique cōgēs?
phrases.english: have you no pity for me? will you drive me to my death in the end?

phrases.latin: hujus igitur bellī ego particeps et socius et adjūtor esse cōgor …?
phrases.english: am I, then, to be forced to be a partner, an ally and a helper in this war …?
The law will force him to marry her.

sources: Lewis & Short: cogo · Lewis & Short: compello
